question: Is there evidence that the 2019 SP-14 pump root cause could repeat on P-4101A at SP-12?
expected_answer: Yes, but it is not confirmed. SP-14 shares the P-4101A/B pump design. In 2019 the cause was misalignment and soft foot after a motor change, missed by a dial gauge check. At SP-12 the trips also started after a motor replacement, only a dial gauge check was done with no soft foot check, and the spectra show strong 1x and 2x components pointing to misalignment or a bent shaft.

evidence.quote: It shares the seawater lift pump design (P-4101A/B) with SP-12, so lessons from SP-14 pump failures apply to SP-12.
Misalignment after the motor replacement, made worse by soft foot, overloaded the bearings.
No soft foot check was done because the feeler gauge set was on the other platform.
which points to misalignment or a bent shaft rather than bearing defects alone

question: Why do the repeated P-4101A trips matter for the firewater system on SP-12?
expected_answer: The seawater lift pumps P-4101A/B also feed the firewater ring main jockey supply. With P-4101A out and P-4101B vibrating more, redundancy on seawater lift is effectively lost, and a low pressure alarm on the jockey supply occurred on 2026-09-09.

evidence.quote: Seawater lift pumps P-4101A/B for cooling and firewater jockey supply.
Low pressure alarm on the firewater ring main jockey supply, which is fed from the seawater lift header.
but redundancy on seawater lift is effectively lost
